ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Preventive Visit — Rachel Carson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Adult preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Ms. Carson returns for her yearly preventive visit, in her fifth ribociclib cycle and four months into letrozole. The cold in July settled in about a week without antibiotics. She has mild morning stiffness in her knees, eased by walking, and occasional hot flashes at night. She finished the draft of her book last month and is now revising it. She completed the health risk assessment before the visit. [S]

tr.td: Left breast cancer after lumpectomy and radiation, on letrozole, ribociclib, and zoledronic acid; low bone mass; knee osteoarthritis
Letrozole 2.5 mg daily; ribociclib 400 mg on days 1 to 21 of each cycle; zoledronic acid every six months; vitamin D3 1000 units daily; acetaminophen as needed

Follow-up: Hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV results by portal message. Second zoster dose in two to six months. Survivorship visit in three months; next zoledronic acid infusion in December; mammogram six to twelve months after radiation. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She has named a health care agent, a close friend, and completed a written health care directive today, now scanned into the chart. Her first instruction is that she is always to be told the truth about her condition, directly and in plain words, and that her clinicians must never withhold a diagnosis or a result from her or tell it to others first. Her treatment is curative in intent. If the cancer returned, she would want treatment that let her keep working and living independently; she would not want resuscitation or prolonged life support if recovery to independent life were not expected. [S]
